title: Neurologic Disorders
description: Clinical and electroneurodiagnostic correlations to various physical conditions and disease states which are commonly dealt with in neurodiagnostic technology are covered in this course. The relationship of technologists to various medical specialties (including neurology, neurosurgery, pathology, radiology, internal medicine, and psychiatry) is emphasized. This course is designed for students enrolled in the Neurodiagnostic Technology Program.
outcomes: Students will be able to recognize the clinical signs and electrographic correlations with infectious disorders, brain tumors, metabolic and/or toxicencephalopathies, headaches, degenerative disorders, psychiatric disorders, cerebrovascular disorders and neonatal disorders.
Students will be able to recognize and identify the various epilepsy syndromes and specific types of seizure disorders with the corresponding electroencephalographic patterns.
Students will be able to understand the antiepileptic medications and their effects.
objectives: Explain and contrast the neuronal basis of normal and abnormal electroencephalographic (EEG) waveforms.
Describe, compare and contrast epilepsy and seizure.
Classify a seizure based on information obtained from a patient history and based on the International System.
Correlate the psychological and social factors encountered by an epileptic person.
Explain the etiology, clinical manifestations, medications of choice, EEG patterns, and prognosis of the major seizure disorders and epileptic syndromes.
Describe the necessary aid for a patient having a seizure.
Differentiate coma and related levels of consciousness, as well as the clinical correlations which may cause those conditions.
Associate EEG correlations with decreased levels of consciousness.
Compare and contrast the clinical signs, EEG correlations, major drugs and treatments with the major psychiatric disorders first evident in infancy, childhood, adolescence, and adults.

Distinguish the clinical signs and EEG correlations with vascular disorders; space-occupying lesions; infective, toxic, metabolic, and degenerative disorders; and common neonatal abnormalities of the brain.
Describe the major diagnostic procedures used for the central nervous system and how they relate to the results obtained from electroneurodiagnostic testing.
Recognize the clinical signs and EEG correlations with headache, including vascular, (i.e. migraine and cluster) tension, and inflammatory.
Recognize the EEG correlations with decreased levels of consciousness.
content: Major psychiatric disorders across the lifespan
Cerebrovascular disorders including cerebrovascular accident/stroke (CVA) and transient ischemic attack (TIA)
Brain space occupying lesions, including tumors, arteriovenous malformations (AVM) and abscesses
Infective disorders including bacterial, viral, parasitic, fungal and delayed-onset syndromes

Common neonatal abnormalities including hyaline membrane disease, hypoxia, fetal cardiac anomalies, infective disorders, thermoregulative dysfunctions, hyperbilirubinemia, intraventricular hemorrhage and seizure activity
Headaches including vascular (i.e. migraine and cluster), tension and inflammatory
Trauma and coma including levels of consciousness
Treatment options including medications of choice
assignments: Professional journals related to neurology and neurodiagnostic technology including: Journal of Clinical Neurology and Neurodiagnostic Journal
Reports on neurology, neurologic disorders (i.e. epilepsy) and neurological testing
Responses to questions from course textbook and instructor-generated handouts
Reports on neurology, neurologic disorders and neurological testing
Compare and contrast seizure and epilepsy.
Recognize the electroencephalographic correlations with decreased levels of activity.
Explain the major diagnostic procedures used for the CNS and how they related to the results obtained from electroneurodiagnostic testing.
